neighbours.label: the '-p' piece that starts the second part of a hyphenated compound (agenda-pushing, back-pedaling)
fire: Voters grew tired of the endless fist-pumping rallies.
The memo was full of chest-puffing claims.
Office hen-pecking drove him to quit.
Her joke got a lot of rib-poking from friends.
The budget was padded with vote-plucking giveaways.
The campaign relied on cheap news-peddling.
quiet: Voters grew tired of the endless fist-waving rallies.
The memo was full of chest-beating claims.
Office nit-picking drove him to quit.
Her joke got a lot of eye-rolling from friends.
The budget was padded with vote-buying giveaways.
Critics mocked the minister's U-turn on taxes.
The campaign relied on cheap fear-mongering.

notes: card: '-p' x4 (agenda-pushing, back-pedaling) and Cyrillic 'еп'/'уп'/'оп' (боеприпасов, полупроводник): a p-initial second element of a compound. Tested in English only. 'nit-picking' near miss may leak if '-p' is split there.
